chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the deceased leaves two brothers, they are brothers with the deceased; they both block the mother from the third [share]. And if there was one, he would not block the mother. And he (peace be upon him) said: When there are four sisters, they block the mother from the third because they are in the position of the two brothers. And if there were three, they would not block [her].

key_terms.حَجَبَ: To block or exclude from inheritance, reducing the share of a closer heir

ai.seo_question: How do siblings block the mother from her one-third share in Islamic inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of 'hijb' (blocking) in Shia inheritance jurisprudence, specifically addressing the mother's share when accompanied by paternal siblings. It establishes a precise numerical threshold: two brothers or four sisters reduce the mother's one-third share to one-sixth, while a single brother or three sisters do not trigger this reduction. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific count of siblings as a condition for altering the parent's fixed portion, distinguishing it from other schools of thought.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from sa’ad Bin Abu Khalaf, from Abu Al Abbas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the deceased leaves two brothers, so they are brothers with the deceased, they both veil the mother from the third. And if there was one, he would not veil the mother’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When there are four sisters, they would block the mother from the third because they are at the statues of the two brothers, and if there were three sisters, they would not be blocking (the mother from the third)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sa‘d ibn abu Khalaf from abu al-‘Abbas who has narrated the following: “Abu "Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, "

If a deceased leaves behind two brothers, they are considered more than two brothers of the deceased and they bar the mother from one-third. If there is one brother he does not bar the mother.’ He (the Imam) said, "If there are four sisters they bar the mother from one-third because they are like two brothers but if there are three sisters they do not bar the mother’s share.’”
